text:
Florida has controlled more of the play so far. At five on five FLA has taken 52% of the expected goals, while VAN sits at 42%, and the gap shows up in the per-60 numbers: FLA creates 3.23 expected goals and allows 3.11, against 2.53 created and 3.64 allowed for VAN. The model expects 4.08 goals for FLA tonight and 2.87 for VAN. The special teams matchup to watch is FLA's power play, which generates 1.42 expected goals a game, against a VAN penalty kill that allows 1.03. FLA has taken 5.29 penalties a game, which keeps handing opponents chances, but VAN's own power play creates only 0.49.

In net, Kevin Lankinen is the projected VAN starter, and he is at -11.11 goals saved above expected this season with a .780 save percentage, after -20.31 last season. Jacob Markstrom is the projected FLA starter, at +2.49 this season (.904) after -15.98 last year. The edge is clearly Florida's, though Markstrom's sample is only five games.

Form points the same way. VAN is 0-5-0 in its last five with 36% of the expected goals, and it never won the chance battle in that stretch, though it came close against the Islanders at 50%. FLA is 2-2-1 with 52%, and it had more expected goals in four of those five games. The model likes Sam Reinhart to score (46%) and Matthew Tkachuk for two or more points (46%), with Brady Tkachuk at 36% to score. For VAN, Jake DeBrusk (28%) is the likeliest to find the net.
